drhp.expansion: The annual report discloses no capacity, capex or expansion project. The only forward-looking operational statement is that the company is being revived by the new management following the NCLT-approved resolution plan, that operations will start any time soon, and that the MD&A segment will be provided from the current financial year onwards. Under the resolution plan the company undertook a reduction of capital and issued new shares to M/s Vision Textile in consideration of funds infused by that entity, leaving the promoter with 97.88% of the equity and the public with 2.12%.

litigation.note: Not determinable from the annual-report bundle: the contingent-liability note, the auditor's report and the CARO annexure are not routed to this reader, so no litigation evidence was available. Absence here is OUR coverage gap, not a statement that the company has no litigation.

drhp.mdna: No demand or outlook commentary is given: management states only that the company is being revived by the new management and that operations will start any time soon, with the MD&A segment to be provided from the current financial year onwards.
drhp.one_liner: Indus Fila Limited is a Bengaluru-based company emerging from a completed IBC resolution process, now 97.88% owned by promoter M/s Vision Textile, which is reviving it ahead of a restart of operations.

promoters.name: M/s Vision Textile
promoters.role: Promoter holding 97.88% of the equity (public shareholding 2.12%) after the capital reduction and fresh share issue made against funds it infused under the NCLT-approved resolution plan; leads the new management reviving the company's operations.

risks.note: Management says only that the company is being revived by the new management and that "operations of the company will start any time soon"; there is no operating business, and MD&A segment disclosure is deferred to the current financial year, so the restart timeline and its execution remain entirely unproven.
risks.risk: Company is not yet operational — revival is unproven

risks.note: An operational creditor's IBC application was admitted by the NCLT, Bengaluru on 20 February 2018 with a moratorium; a resolution plan was approved on 10 May 2019 and proceedings closed on 22 April 2022. The company's entire capital structure and ownership rest on implementation of that plan.
During the moratorium the company was delisted by both BSE and NSE, so shareholders' ability to trade the stock depends on regulatory and exchange processes rather than on operating performance.

M/s Vision Textile (Promoter) holds 97.88% of the equity while public shareholding stands at 2.12%, following the capital reduction and fresh issue under the NCLT orders — leaving minority holders with negligible influence and negligible float.
risks.risk: Extreme promoter concentration and minimal public float

risks.note: The company states it has designed a risk management framework and formulated a risk management policy supported by the Board, management and the Committee, but no risks-and-concerns discussion or risk register is disclosed, so investors cannot yet see which operating risks are being tracked or how.
risks.risk: Risk framework is policy-stage, with oversight concentrated in the Board and one committee
